messages:
maria: Quick heads-up — proposing a small-ish schema change to console_telemetry to make routing/debugging and quota reporting easier. Suggest adding a new column route_label TEXT and a quota_profile ENUM (light, standard, enterprise) so we can avoid parsing a JSON blob in dashboards. Thoughts?

jon: +1 to making dashboards simpler. JSON parsing in queries is a perf hit. How big is the backfill though?

maria: Estimate ~120M rows over last 90 days (only ingest table). Backfill would be an offline job that writes to a new column. Plan: add columns nullable, run backfill, then set NOT NULL and add constraints.

kevin: A couple of questions:
- Do we map existing route_id -> route_label via existing route_metadata table?
- For quota_profile, do we derive from quota_profiles table or from the route config snapshot?

maria: Yes to both. We'll join route_metadata.route_id -> label in the backfill. For quota_profile we'll use the active route_config snapshot at event_time; fallback to 'standard' if missing.

ashley: Need to consider consumer compatibility. Event consumers (billing, alerts) read console_telemetry directly — we should keep reads unaffected. I suggest feature-flagging consumer changes and not switching anything until backfill is done and we land a compat layer.

maria: Agreed. Migration will be transparent: no consumer reads will change. We'll add columns and populate; then follow with a metric rollout to start reading new fields in dashboards.

jon: Implementation nit: prefer a lightweight enum via PostgreSQL type vs varchar with check? enums are faster for joins but harder to alter if we add profile types later.

kevin: We can do a text column + check constraint now, and later migrate to an enum if needed. Or use a small lookup table quota_profile(name) and FK. That keeps evolution easier.

maria: I prefer lookup table + FK. Easier to extend and safer for backfills.

schema-bot: Migration draft created: mr/4523-add-route-label-and-quota-profile — created by maria. Reviewers: jon, kevin, ashley. CI: pg-migrations, integration-tests.

jon: For backfill approach: propose a streaming backfill that reads day's partitions and writes in batches so we avoid long table locks. Something like:
```sql
-- pseudocode
ALTER TABLE console_telemetry ADD COLUMN route_label text;
ALTER TABLE console_telemetry ADD COLUMN quota_profile_id bigint;
-- run idempotent batch script: select id, route_id, event_time from console_telemetry where route_label is null limit 10000; join route_metadata/event_snapshots; update console_telemetry set route_label=..., quota_profile_id=... where id in (...);
```

ashley: Make sure to add an index on route_label for dashboard queries: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON console_telemetry (route_label). And for quota_profile_id too.

maria: Yep, will do CONCURRENTLY indexes. Also planning to use logical replication for a short period so consumers can switch reads to a read-replica that has the new columns before we set NOT NULL.

kevin: Any SLO/regression risk? Backfill CPU and IO could spike. Suggest running in low-traffic windows and a kill-switch to pause. We should also add a quota on backfill worker to limit DB connections.

maria: Add runbook step for kill-switch and DB ticket if latency climbs. We'll gate on 99th percentile write latency not exceeding 150ms baseline + 30ms.

jon: Dashboards: Console metrics team needs a mapping table change in grafana queries. We'll coordinate with them — maybe add a short-lived view that exposes old JSON + new flattened columns to make query migration gradual.

ashley: Good idea. Also update telemetry ingestion docs and the schema registry so auditing services know the change.

maria: I'll open a separate docs PR. Plan/next steps:
- MR with ADD COLUMN + lookup table + indexes (nonblocking)
- Backfill job (batch + streaming fallback) with kill-switch & connection caps
- Integration tests + perf run on staging replica
- Dashboards migrate to new columns via view, then switch consumers
- Make columns NOT NULL and add FK/constraints

kevin: Sounds solid. Can you include estimated wall time for backfill in the MR? Helps SRE schedule maintenance windows.

maria: Yep, initial guess 8–12 hours for full 90-day backfill with batched workers, but will test on a 10% sample to refine.

jon: One more: consider adding a tiny 'route_label_hash' int4 computed column for faster equality filters (index on int). Might help at scale.

maria: Noted — will prototype.

ashley: If everyone is ok, I'll add myself as release owner to coordinate dashboards and docs.

maria: Thanks — I'll post the MR link when ready. Ping me for review threads. :thumbsup:
